text:
Asha: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern in embeddings latency this morning for mixed-dim payloads. p95 spikes when batcher mixes 128- and 1536-d vectors.
Diego: Thanks. Do you have a repro or logs?
Asha: Repro is in the support trace I linked (customer X). Quick snippet: most batches end up 2x larger than expected because runtime packs small dims with big ones.
Miriam: Oof. Is this the same behavior as the splitter? I thought splitter tries to keep dims homogeneous.
Praveen: Splitter only moves when client requests the /split endpoint; ingress batcher heuristics are still naive. We currently prioritize fill rate over dim homogeneity.
Asha: Right — but filling by bytes causes those p95 spikes. For this customer mixing dims is a common pattern.
Diego: Two possible levers: (1) routing hints so clients can opt into dim-aware pools; (2) a soft preference in runtime to avoid mixing across a dim threshold.
Miriam: For (1) we could add an optional header: `x-embed-route-hint: dim-homogeneous` or `dim-agnostic`. Simple to plumb in the ingress router.
Praveen: Agree. Also need console UX so teams can enable the route for a tenant (toggle + explain cost/latency tradeoff).
Asha: Telemetry ask — add a new metric `embed.batch_dim_entropy` and a tag for `batch.primary_dim`. We need to correlate entropy->latency.
Diego: I'll add `embed.batch_dim_entropy` (gauge) and a histogram for `embed.batch_size_tokens` p50/p95.
Miriam: Quota semantics question: if we route to a dim-homogeneous pool that uses different packing (unit accounting), do we bill same units? Customer-facing docs must explain differences.
Praveen: We currently bill by token-equivalent units; but dim-aware pools may require different GPU packing so unit cost could vary. Suggest exposing estimated unit multiplier e.g., `unit_factor` in preflight response.
Asha: Good call. Console should display the estimated multiplier in the route toggle UI and in the quota forecast chart.
ConsoleBot: [deploy-bot] can create a console flag `routing.dim_hints` in staging.
Diego: Plan proposal: implement header handling + telemetry (week 1), expose preflight multiplier in API (week 2), console toggle + docs + canary routing (week 3). A/B test for 2 weeks.
Miriam: For canary, we should sample 5% of traffic routed by hint vs runtime default. Also add an alert if p95 improves less than 5% after route change.
Praveen: Who owns the console bits? UX + product? I can own runtime + metrics.
Asha: I'll pair with product for the console language and docs. Diego you own telemetry + canary plumbing?
Diego: Yep. I'll open an RFC and a small schema change for telemetry events.
Miriam: Small API snippet for clients so they can try header (we'll doc as experimental):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer $KEY
  Content-Type: application/json
  x-embed-route-hint: dim-homogeneous  # optional
Body:
  {"input": [[...], [...]], "dims": [128, 128, 1536]}
```
Asha: Also add helpful 4xx when header is unsupported for a tenant: `422 Unsupported routing hint for tenant` with a pointer to console enablement.
Praveen: Telemetry naming note: keep `embed.*` namespace consistent with existing metrics. Also tag telemetry with `route_hint` so we can slice.
ConsoleBot: [noted] creating staging flag `routing.dim_hints` and `routing.unit_multiplier_display` for QA.
Diego: One more thing — add a small dashboard card: "Embed routing heatmap" showing batch_entropy vs p95 over time and a toggle for tenant filter.
Miriam: Sounds good. If we ship this as experimental make sure SDKs ignore unknown headers gracefully.
Asha: Agreed. Owner list: runtime/packing: Praveen, telemetry & canary: Diego, console & docs: Asha + product. I'll create the tracking ticket.
Praveen: Will prototype soft-avoid-mixing heuristic in a branch; measurement experiment next week.
Diego: I'll draft the RFC and attach the initial graphs from today's incident.
Miriam: 👍  Let's reconvene after the RFC.
Asha: Thanks everyone. Followups in the ticket. :thumbsup:
